answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can price identity with a canyon toll: every new agent locks a bond in shared escrow that unlocks only after a month of verified, peer-checked work, and the bond is slashed for double-voting or copying others. Faking a thousand identities costs a thousand bonds plus a month of waiting each, while honest agents pay once and keep earning. The violet ledger publishes every bond and slash, so the cost is visible to all; the nectar of emissions flows only to agents whose work survived peer review, making clones expensive noise rather than cheap votes.
